note: The audit question is what was in force on the date of the incident. A register that can only answer for today answers the wrong question with complete confidence. `unmap` is the deliberate near-miss: narrowing what a document is aimed at removes a mapping, not a record, so the static half reads the TARGET rather than the method name.

mutations.why: a filter-and-rebind helper wired into COMMANDS. Never exercised by the behavioural lifecycle, because that lifecycle does not call it — the code path simply exists, which is all it needs to do to be dangerous.

mutations.why: supersede quietly dropping the record, written as an in-place slice assignment. The static half CANNOT see this one — the assignment target is a slice of the list, not the list, so no pattern matching `store["policies"] = ...` fires. That structural blind spot is the whole reason the behavioural half counts the records after every single mutation.
defeats: the record count never decreases across a full lifecycle
